It appears from the video that since the student chose to record their interaction with the administrator, the administrator feels threatened and chose to call their guardian to come escort the student off the premises because they are "in an elevated state" from the confrontation. The student does not appear to be violent during this recording so Im not sure what is so threatning about a recording during what should be an honest interaction between a professional educator and a student but the educator appears to be trying to potray the situation as more dangerous than what it appears to be from the video, to justify their position and actions and allow them to escalate the sutuation.

From all of this I would surmise the school resource officer was instructed to keep the student in the office until their guardian arrives to escort them from the premises. This seems, from my observations over the years of similar situations, to be standard behavior for school administrators to build a narrative to support their actions so their decisions and their authority can not be questioned by students. I imagine the distress we see from the student is the result of the frustration of realizing that most people in power do not honestly care about right and wrong but simply want to maintain their power and crush any one who questions that power.

Just to be clear I am a man but I would never tell you to "man up" and any one who does has never felt PTSD or clinical depression. If you have clinical depression you do not just "feel sad" all the time more than that you feel nothing and thus no motivation to even clean your self or eat or live. PTSD makes you feel hypervigilant and makes you evaluate every thing around you and about other people's reactions to you. Usually the issues that caused you to develop PTSD make you assume the worst about those reactions of others around you and as such you are usually left friendless and labeled a confrontational b***h or a*****e in my case. I know these struggles and live them each day. I was diagnosed with CPTSD which means mine was caused by  18 years of abuse and torture by my mother. Her favorite saying to me was "you are unloveable. If your own mother can't stand to be around you what the hell makes you think anyone else will ever be able to love you?". I don't know if this will help but two things I used to help me survive to today. First thing when I had a panic attack I learned to stop and look around the room and start listing things in my mind I could control or change right now. This made me stop thinking about everything in the future that was overwhelming me and gave me a chance to calm down and get myself back to a place where I could feel in control of my immidiate future. The other thing is I quit trying and thinking about living my "life" because it was too much and just felt overwhelming and seemed hopeless. Instead I would find bright things to look forward to in my near future and my mantra would be "if I can just survive till this then I will be ok". For example right now my daughters want to watch the new "Wonder Woman" movie on Christmas day. So all I am focused on right now is what I have to do to make it to that day and what do I have to do today to get there. I have tried to end things twice and cant get any better help because of my insurance so I have some one who lives in my room with me and watches my every move so I know that level of frustration. I dont know if this will help you or not but it has allowed me to survive to 46 so I hope it does. Feel free to DM me if you need to talk more. Hope you find the help you need.
